judged_text: deleteEvent has the same regression: the fallback now searches for externalId === externalCalendarId (undefined when not passed) instead of using event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Deleting a booking without an explicit externalCalendarId resolves calendarId to undefined and the delete fails, leaving orphaned calendar events for bookings whose references lack externalCalendarId — the exact case the old fallback covered.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` (same pattern also appears in `updateEvent`). When `externalCalendarId` is not provided, the `.find(... cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against `undefined`, so it will typically return `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` has entries. This removes the prior fallback behavior (previously it used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can make the delete call target an undefined calendarId, risking failed deletes/orphaned events for references lacking `externalCalendarId`.
